race_context: The Evansville Vanderburgh School Corporation (EVSC) serves Evansville and Vanderburgh County; WNIN describes it as serving more than 21,000 students and as Indiana's third-largest district {wnin_officers}. The district lists 22 elementary, 8 middle and 7 high schools plus district-wide programs {evsc_board}.

The board has seven members, elected by voters across Evansville and Vanderburgh County {wnin_officers}. Seats are designated by district (District 1, District 2, etc.) or at large, and WNIN reports that voters across the county vote in the District 2 race {wnin_d2_challengers}.

Board president Mike Duckworth said the board hired superintendent Darla Hoover, who started in July 2025 {wnin_d2_incumbents}. In January 2026 the board chose Duckworth as president, Melissa Moore as vice president and Amy DeVries as secretary {wnin_officers}.

Four seats are on the 2026 ballot, with 10 candidates on the ballot after the June 18 filing deadline {wnin_ballot}. The state list shows District 2 as 'vote for 1', but WNIN reports that two District 2 seats are up and that voters will choose two of the four District 2 candidates {wnin_ballot}{wnin_d2_challengers}.

District 1: incumbent Chris Kiefer is unopposed {wnin_ballot}. District 2: incumbents Mike Duckworth and David Hollingsworth are running for reelection against Lindsey Patterson and Ken Colbert {wnin_d2_challengers}. At Large: incumbent Melissa Moore faces Steve Ary, Andy Guarino, Brian Murphy and Alan Goad {wnin_atlarge}.

Partisan labels: Steve Ary is the only candidate listed with a party (Republican) and WNIN describes him as the first partisan EVSC board candidate under a new state law; the other nine filed as nonpartisan {wnin_ballot}{wnin_atlarge}. A second Republican filer, Ryan Owens, withdrew during the grace period {wnin_ballot}.

Safety audit (December 2025): on Dec. 15, 2025 the board approved a $215,000 district-wide security assessment of all 40 EVSC buildings, policies and crisis procedures by National School Safety and Security Services, the first district-wide study since 2008 {wnin_audit}.

Property-tax law (2025–2026): WNIN reported that EVSC 'will lose millions of dollars' under the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) {wnin_atlarge}. This guide did not find an EVSC budget document stating the amount.
Student devices (2025–2026): candidates discussed the state-required limits on cell phones and other devices in schools {wnin_atlarge}{wnin_d2_challengers}.

Forums and interviews: WNIN published interviews with the at-large candidates (Sept. 23), the District 2 incumbents (Oct. 1) and the District 2 challengers (Oct. 2) {wnin_atlarge}{wnin_d2_incumbents}{wnin_d2_challengers}. This guide did not find a 2026 candidate forum or newspaper questionnaire for this race.

Key differences: at-large challengers differ on priorities, from safety and device limits (Ary, Goad) to career education and employee health benefits (Murphy) and enrollment and teacher pay (Guarino) {wnin_atlarge}. In District 2 the incumbents point to their records, while Colbert criticizes the board on transparency and Patterson says she would first learn how the board works {wnin_d2_incumbents}{wnin_d2_challengers}.

background: BallotReady lists him as faculty program chair for criminal justice at Ivy Tech Community College {ballotready_kiefer}.
BallotReady lists his current District 1 term as running through Dec. 31, 2026, and shows him as a candidate for the same seat in 2022 {ballotready_kiefer}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a nonpartisan candidate and has no opponent on the ballot {wnin_ballot}{in_list}.

items: Speaking about the district-wide security study in December 2025, he said its aim is to prevent incidents and that a comprehensive study helps the district respond quickly if a serious situation occurs {wnin_audit}.

gaps: No 2026 interview, questionnaire or campaign website found; WNIN's candidate coverage did not profile the uncontested District 1 race.
Seen only in search snippets (unverified): a Courier & Press report that the withdrawn Republican filer was running for District 1.
No campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 2 trustee seeking a third term {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
background: Retired ironworker who also drives a school bus part-time for EVSC {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
PTA area council president and former vice president; he says he has received PTA awards, including a lifetime achievement award {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Has served two terms (eight years) on the board {wnin_d2_challengers}.

items: Says safety is his first priority {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Wants reading scores to rise; says the district has met some goals but must improve {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Says he wants to keep politics out of schools and does not want to be labeled as one party's member {wnin_d2_incumbents}.

on_incumbent: Says the board has 'achieved some of our goals' but 'we need to get better,' and that his record 'speaks for itself' {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
plans: Says he would continue his PTA work and use the board seat to talk with students, staff and bus drivers in district buildings {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
gaps: WNIN's interview did not cover his views on the budget, the 2025 property-tax law, staffing or the device policy.
No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Challenger for one of the two District 2 seats; a local business owner who has criticized the board on transparency {wnin_d2_challengers}.
background: Owns a consignment shop in Evansville and co-founded the Indiana Freedom Caucus, according to WNIN {wnin_d2_challengers}.
Co-hosts the podcast 'Republicans in Bad Standing' {wnin_d2_challengers}.

items: WNIN reported that he criticizes the board for lacking transparency and says his public-records requests have gone unanswered for years {wnin_d2_challengers}.

In posts signed with his name on the Telegram channel 'ColbertReport', he says he backs 'Complete Transparency and a #studentfirst agenda' and says the current administration is not transparent about federal funding {colbert_telegram}.
In a post on the same channel, he linked falling ACT scores to the board's past curriculum votes {colbert_telegram}.

on_incumbent: WNIN reported he argued that incumbents benefit from name recognition {wnin_d2_challengers}.
His channel's posts urge voters to replace current board members whom he calls 'career politicians' {colbert_telegram}.
gaps: Did not respond to WNIN's interview requests, per WNIN; positions here come from WNIN's summary and his own Telegram posts, which carry no calendar dates.

WNIN's article also reports that he and his podcast co-host were removed from the state and county Republican Party and that he faces a recent bench warrant related to an attempt to file as a Republican in another race; this guide could not confirm the details from court or party records.
No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and EVSC graduate challenging for one of the two District 2 seats {wnin_d2_challengers}.
background: Born and raised in Evansville; attended Delaware, Evans and North schools {wnin_d2_challengers}.
Parent of students in the district, including a North High School senior {wnin_d2_challengers}.

items: Called the district's security study a good idea {wnin_d2_challengers}.
On the state-required device policy, said the district's 'hands are probably tied a little bit' because it is state law {wnin_d2_challengers}.
Says she is running nonpartisan because 'politics needs to stay out of public education' {wnin_d2_challengers}.

on_incumbent: Told WNIN she needs more information before forming opinions on specific board policies {wnin_d2_challengers}.
plans: Her first priority would be learning how the board works and getting to know the superintendent and community {wnin_d2_challengers}.
gaps: No stated positions found on the budget, the 2025 property-tax law, staffing or academics.
No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 2 trustee and board president, with 26 non-consecutive years on the board {wnin_officers}{wnin_d2_incumbents}.
background: Retired from the sheriff's department in 1997, later worked as a local representative for U.S. Senators Richard Lugar and Dan Coats, and held city posts including water superintendent {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Was a Little League commissioner for 35 years {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Chosen board president in January 2026, his sixth time in the role {wnin_officers}.

items: Describes the district's budget as 'about a third of a billion dollar budget' and says careful use of taxpayer money is important {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Calls safety a 'main priority' and says the district works with city and county police {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Says the district is studying its facilities so it can spend money appropriately, and cites the Bosse High School overpass and athletic upgrades as accomplishments {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Wants to study redistricting and bus routes, saying early-morning and late-afternoon rides in the dark are 'dangerous' {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Points to the district's focus on students reading by third grade {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
Says he has always run nonpartisan and that politics should be kept separate from the board; says vacancies should be filled by the board rather than party committees {wnin_d2_incumbents}.

on_incumbent: Says the board's main job is hiring the superintendent and setting policy, and that he does not micromanage {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
plans: Wants to review technology policies in light of state cell-phone rules {wnin_d2_incumbents}.
gaps: No stated position found on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) or a referendum.
No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Military veteran and maintenance supervisor challenging the at-large incumbent {wnin_atlarge}.
background: Served 14 years in the military; works as a maintenance tech supervisor for a property management company {wnin_atlarge}.

items: Says 'District security studies I'm all for and agree with' and raised concerns about safety in special-needs classrooms {wnin_atlarge}.
Wants better pay and support for teachers, who he says 'aren't being taken care of good enough' {wnin_atlarge}.
Supports the cell phone and gaming device ban, with medical exceptions {wnin_atlarge}.

on_incumbent: Says families feel unheard and that some trustees 'weren't paying attention' {wnin_atlarge}.
gaps: Answered WNIN's questions by email; no recorded interview, campaign website or other coverage found.
No stated positions found on the budget or the 2025 property-tax law.
No endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Former EVSC trustee and retired principal seeking to return to the board {wnin_atlarge}.
background: Was a principal for 17 years and an assistant principal for 10; holds master's degrees in adult education and special education {wnin_atlarge}.
Served on the EVSC board for about nine years, leaving four years ago; has served on the EVSC Foundation board and as president of Evansville Retired Teachers {wnin_atlarge}.
Has worked as a substitute in EVSC for more than 115 days over the past four years {wnin_atlarge}.

items: Lists the cell phone policy as his first priority {wnin_atlarge}.
Wants to 'make sure we don't lose any kids' amid competition from vouchers and charter schools {wnin_atlarge}.
Points to past board action removing a $60,000 salary cap, which he calls 'the biggest pay raise EVSC had ever given teachers at one time' {wnin_atlarge}.
Supports the outside security review, saying 'I thought it was a good study' {wnin_atlarge}.

on_incumbent: Calls incumbent Melissa Moore 'a very good person' and says he is running to return to the board, not against her {wnin_atlarge}.
gaps: WNIN's article gives his past tenure both as two terms plus a partial year and as 'nine years' without reconciling them.
No stated positions found on the budget or the 2025 property-tax law.
No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Home builder and Marine Corps veteran focused on career education and employee benefits {wnin_atlarge}.
background: Has lived in Evansville since 2000; served in the U.S. Marine Corps; runs a family home-building business and has done real estate development {wnin_atlarge}.
Taught career trades in the Dallas area and works on EVSC construction projects {wnin_atlarge}.

items: Says the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) will 'severely limit and restrict' school funding and expects referendums to be the likely response {wnin_atlarge}.
Wants to expand career education and the Southwest Indiana Career and Technical Center {wnin_atlarge}.
Criticizes IREAD and ILEARN testing for pushing teachers to 'teach to a test' {wnin_atlarge}.
Wants equal health-care options for all EVSC employees, including custodians and paraprofessionals {wnin_atlarge}.
Supports the comprehensive safety study {wnin_atlarge}.
Supports no screens in classrooms and would extend limits to Chromebooks {wnin_atlarge}.

on_incumbent: Says he offers 'a fresh perspective' and that board members may not fully understand construction projects {wnin_atlarge}.
plans: Wants the board to listen more to students {wnin_atlarge}.
gaps: No campaign website, endorsements or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent at-large trustee and board vice president, first elected in 2022 {wnin_officers}.
background: Navy veteran and life coach; Evansville native and Bosse High School graduate {wnin_atlarge}.
Elected to the board in 2022; board vice president since January 2026 {wnin_officers}.

items: Lists student success and literacy as priorities, citing 'increasing of literacy scores' {wnin_atlarge}.
Says she objected by email to a short graduation ceremony at one school and that this year's ceremonies were longer and more inclusive {wnin_atlarge}.

on_incumbent: Says she is running again 'because the work is not done' and that new members need time to get acclimated to the role {wnin_atlarge}.
endorsements_finance: WNIN reported that the county Republican Party has criticized county Democrats for supporting her {wnin_atlarge}.
gaps: WNIN's interview did not cover her views on the budget, the 2025 property-tax law, safety or staffing.
No campaign website or campaign finance reports found.

candidates.summary: Republican challenger for the at-large seat; WNIN calls him the first partisan EVSC board candidate {wnin_ballot}.
background: Says he is a foster parent whose children attend EVSC schools {wnin_atlarge}.
Says he previously ran for county party chairman {wnin_atlarge}.
path_to_ballot: Filed as a Republican under a new state law allowing party labels in school board races {wnin_ballot}{in_list}.
Explaining the label, he said, 'I believe it's important for people to know where you stand' {wnin_atlarge}.

items: Lists safety as his top priority and wants policy based on the district's safety audit; supports weapons detection systems while saying 'It's not a solution to everything' {wnin_atlarge}.
Says he is '100-percent for the banning of those devices' {wnin_atlarge}.
Wants 'social issues' kept out of classrooms {wnin_atlarge}.
Says foster children often arrive unable to read and 'We have to do better' {wnin_atlarge}.

on_incumbent: Criticizes the status quo, saying 'if you always do what you've always done, you'll always get what you've always got' {wnin_atlarge}.
plans: Wants to help foster children and students facing bullying, academic struggles and safety issues {wnin_atlarge}.
endorsements_finance: County Republican Chair Kyhle Moers said the party plans to support his campaign with door knocking, phone banking and mail {wnin_ballot}.
gaps: How the party label was obtained (petition or party certification) was not described in sources found.
No stated positions found on the budget or the 2025 property-tax law.
No campaign website or campaign finance reports found.
